draft.name: kdigo_aki_creatinine_rise_0.3_48h
draft.sql: WITH cr AS (SELECT l.hadm_id, l.charttime, l.valuenum FROM labevents l JOIN d_labitems d ON l.itemid = d.itemid WHERE d.label = 'Creatinine' AND d.fluid = 'Blood' AND l.valuenum IS NOT NULL AND l.hadm_id IS NOT NULL) SELECT DISTINCT a.hadm_id FROM cr a JOIN cr b ON a.hadm_id = b.hadm_id AND b.charttime > a.charttime AND b.charttime <= a.charttime + INTERVAL 48 HOUR AND b.valuenum - a.valuenum >= 0.3 ORDER BY a.hadm_id
assumptions: Serum creatinine is identified as d_labitems label 'Creatinine' with fluid 'Blood' (MIMIC-IV itemid 50912); no other itemids are included.
A rise is computed as a later creatinine value minus an earlier value within the same hadm_id, with the later charttime strictly after and at most 48 hours after the earlier charttime.
The 0.3 mg/dL threshold is applied as an absolute difference (>= 0.3) in valuenum, assumed to be in mg/dL; valueuom is not filtered.
Any earlier measurement in the admission can serve as the baseline; no separate baseline definition is applied.
Lab rows with null valuenum or null hadm_id are excluded.
Only the absolute-rise criterion is implemented; the KDIGO 1.5x-baseline-within-7-days criterion and urine output criteria are not included because the text does not state them.
Admissions meeting the criterion are returned once each, ordered by hadm_id.

draft.name: aki_kdigo_48h
draft.sql: WITH cr AS (SELECT l.hadm_id, l.charttime, l.valuenum FROM labevents l JOIN d_labitems d ON d.itemid = l.itemid WHERE d.label = 'Creatinine' AND d.fluid = 'Blood' AND l.hadm_id IS NOT NULL AND l.charttime IS NOT NULL AND l.valuenum IS NOT NULL) SELECT DISTINCT a.hadm_id FROM cr a JOIN cr b ON b.hadm_id = a.hadm_id AND b.charttime > a.charttime AND b.charttime <= a.charttime + INTERVAL 48 HOUR AND b.valuenum - a.valuenum >= 0.3
assumptions: Serum creatinine is identified by d_labitems rows with label 'Creatinine' and fluid 'Blood', so no hard-coded itemid is used.
A rise is evaluated as a later creatinine minus an earlier creatinine, with the earlier value as baseline; any pair of measurements in the same admission qualifies.
The 48-hour window is inclusive: the later measurement must be after the earlier one and no more than 48 hours after it.
The threshold is a rise of at least 0.3 mg/dL (inequality >= 0.3), using valuenum as recorded; unit conversion is not applied.
Rows with null hadm_id, charttime, or valuenum are excluded.
Only creatinine measurements linked to the same hadm_id are compared, so the rise must occur within one admission.
The urine-output criterion is not used, per the specification.

assumptions: The methods text does not define how diabetes is identified: no ICD-9 or ICD-10 code list, HbA1c or glucose threshold, or medication rule is given, so the criterion cannot be computed without inventing one.

The other stated criteria (age at least 18, ICU stay of at least 24 h, at least seven finger-stick glucose measurements within a 24-hour ICU stay) are not the diabetes criterion and are not implemented here.
Finger-stick glucose itemids in chartevents or labevents are not specified, so that criterion also cannot be implemented from the text alone.
A diabetes ICD code list (for example E10 to E14 in diagnoses_icd) or a stated lab threshold would be needed before a query could be written.

draft.name: KDIGO-style AKI: serum creatinine rise >= 0.3 mg/dL within 48 hours in one admission
draft.sql: WITH cr AS (SELECT l.hadm_id, l.charttime, l.valuenum FROM labevents l JOIN d_labitems d ON l.itemid = d.itemid WHERE lower(d.label) = 'creatinine' AND lower(d.fluid) = 'blood' AND l.hadm_id IS NOT NULL AND l.valuenum IS NOT NULL AND l.charttime IS NOT NULL) SELECT DISTINCT a.hadm_id FROM cr a JOIN cr b ON a.hadm_id = b.hadm_id AND b.charttime > a.charttime AND b.charttime <= a.charttime + INTERVAL 48 HOUR AND b.valuenum - a.valuenum >= 0.3
assumptions: Serum creatinine is identified via d_labitems with label 'Creatinine' and fluid 'Blood' (itemid 50912 in standard MIMIC-IV), not a hand-picked itemid list.
Values are assumed to be in mg/dL, the standard MIMIC-IV unit for blood creatinine. No unit conversion or filter on valueuom is applied.

A rise means a later measurement minus any earlier measurement in the same admission is >= 0.3. The later measurement must be strictly after the earlier one and no more than 48 hours after it (inclusive of 48 h).
Only lab rows linked to a hadm_id are used, so both measurements belong to the same admission.
Rows with null valuenum or null charttime are excluded.
No plausibility limits are applied to creatinine values.

draft.name: aki_kdigo_48h
draft.sql: WITH cr AS (SELECT l.hadm_id, l.charttime, l.valuenum FROM labevents l JOIN d_labitems d ON l.itemid = d.itemid WHERE lower(d.label) = 'creatinine' AND lower(d.fluid) = 'blood' AND l.hadm_id IS NOT NULL AND l.charttime IS NOT NULL AND l.valuenum IS NOT NULL AND (l.valueuom IS NULL OR lower(l.valueuom) = 'mg/dl')) SELECT DISTINCT b.hadm_id FROM cr a JOIN cr b ON a.hadm_id = b.hadm_id AND b.charttime > a.charttime AND b.charttime <= a.charttime + INTERVAL 48 HOUR AND round(b.valuenum - a.valuenum, 6) >= 0.3
assumptions: Serum creatinine is identified through d_labitems as label 'Creatinine' with fluid 'Blood'. This matches by label rather than a hard-coded itemid; in MIMIC-IV it mainly corresponds to itemid 50912.
Only results with valueuom 'mg/dL', or with no unit recorded, are used. They are taken to be in mg/dL.
A rise means a later creatinine value minus an earlier one is >= 0.3 mg/dL. The earlier value does not have to be the lowest value of the admission.
Both measurements must be linked to the same hadm_id. Lab results with no hadm_id are excluded.
'Within 48 hours' means the later measurement is strictly after the earlier one and no more than 48 hours later (inclusive at 48h).
The difference is rounded to 6 decimal places before comparison. This prevents floating-point error from wrongly excluding rises of exactly 0.3.
The urine-output criterion and the 1.5x-baseline-within-7-days criterion are not used, as the specification states.

draft.sql: SELECT NULL::BIGINT AS hadm_id WHERE false
assumptions: The methods text says only 'patients with diabetes' and never says how diabetes was identified.
It gives no ICD-9/ICD-10 code list, for example whether to include 250.x, 249.x, E08-E13 or gestational O24.
It names no laboratory criterion, such as an HbA1c or glucose threshold.
It names no medication criterion, such as insulin or oral hypoglycemics.
It does not say whether diabetes had to be a prior history or a diagnosis in the index admission.
Any of these would mean inventing a code list or threshold, so the criterion cannot be computed as stated.
